related_questions.question: What taxes are exempt in a combat zone?
related_questions.snippet: The Combat Zone Tax Exclusion (CZTE) is a provision that exempts all or a portion of earnings from federal income taxes while a Service member is deployed to a designated combat zone. This can mean more money in your pocket or more to achieve your financial goals.
related_questions.title: COMBAT ZONE TAX EXCLUSION

related_questions.question: What is the maximum income exclusion for combat pay?
related_questions.snippet: The limit for 2023 is $10,011 per month, which consists of $9,786 for the highest enlisted pay and $225 for imminent danger pay. Income excluded from hospitalization after serving in a combat zone is limited to two years from the last month of presence in the combat zone.

related_questions.question: What is military exclusion on taxes?
related_questions.snippet: One of the most notable military tax benefits is the exclusion of combat pay from taxable income. Combat Zone Tax Exclusions (CZTE) ensure that additional income earned in designated combat zones is not subject to federal income tax.
